manifest.description: Clear scam calls with multiple manipulation tactics.
Normal family check-ins and general conversation.
Legitimate retail customer service and ordering.
Legitimate calls from authorities or medical offices.
Legitimate time-sensitive situations (e.g., missed flight, medical appointment).
Emotionally charged but legitimate conversations (e.g., family argument, grieving).
Legitimate requests for privacy (e.g., doctor asking to speak privately).
Complex scams overlapping urgency, isolation, and authority.
Subtle, grooming-like scams (e.g., early stages of romance scam).
